contract.note: Further training released DeepSeek models ordinarily counts as building on its work. One actual derivative satisfies the first branch.

evidence.note: Skywork's repository documents a May 2025 release derived from DeepSeek distilled models. This is a developer disclosure establishing the relevant release and provenance.
The authors' May 2025 report corroborates DeepSeek provenance and released weights. It is not independent verification, but its benchmark claims are unnecessary here.

reviews.rationale: The documented third-party derivative release after January 29, 2025 satisfies the contract's early-resolution rule. The disjunction requires neither proof of rented-GPU deployments nor widespread adoption. No material counterevidence is supplied.

attribution.note: Both assertions are Zitron's own endorsed observations.

semantics.note: Preserves the data-constraint and capability-plateau assertions. The surrounding assertion that the architecture has peaked supports the plateau reading.

contract.note: An approaching constraint on human text and a broad capability plateau are fair ordinary readings. The speaker imposed no fixed inference-compute budget.

evidence.note: Supports an approaching public human-text constraint under continued scaling. It does not establish exhaustion of synthetic, private or multimodal data.
Independent testing shows substantial post-March accuracy gains using the same baseline framework. Greater inference time qualifies efficiency, which the claim did not fix.
Developer measurements report substantial gains across mathematics, science and coding. These supplement independent evidence but are not independent findings; inference compute and sampling vary.
Similar autonomy performance and limited research-task success qualify the breadth of progress. Scaffolding, latency and time limits constrain what these results establish about a general plateau.

reviews.rationale: The approaching human-text constraint is supported on the contract's reading. The broad capability plateau is contradicted by substantial gains on several difficult tasks. METR shows that improvements were uneven, and increased inference compute limits efficiency comparisons, but neither establishes a broad plateau.

attribution.note: Zitron directly endorses both universal negatives.

semantics.note: Preserves the present-tense claims about economic scale and profitable business outcomes.

contract.note: Requiring attributable benefits exceeding costs is fair. Restricting the observation to calendar 2024 is not supplied by the speaker and excludes otherwise relevant outcomes. The trillion-dollar valuation also remains undefined.

evidence.note: Klarna reports AI-related savings, including first-quarter image-production savings, but supplies no complete deployment-cost reconciliation. Annualized company-reported savings do not establish realized net profit.

reviews.rationale: Klarna's disclosure is relevant counterevidence but does not establish benefits exceeding all deployment costs. The packet neither establishes the universal negatives nor supplies a qualifying counterexample. This evidentiary gap remains even without the contract's unjustified calendar-year restriction.

attribution.note: The quoted sentence asserts Zitron's own assessment of existing resources, rights and barriers.

semantics.note: The normalization omits the explicit assertion of unfettered use and access, retaining only non-revocability. The contract restores that material assertion. The sentence describes current barriers rather than predicting termination.

contract.note: Testing practical capacity, license breadth and replacement barriers is an ordinary reading. Separating access from irrevocability and unrestricted use fairly preserves the actual statement.

evidence.note: Microsoft's contemporaneous disclosure supports substantial IP access and infrastructure involvement. It does not establish irrevocability, unrestricted use or negligible replacement barriers.

The October 2025 company disclosure describes changed permissions. Without a reliable historical bridge, it cannot establish the precise January restrictions or practical barriers to replacing GPT and Claude.

reviews.rationale: The packet establishes substantial Microsoft access, but not the asserted breadth and irrevocability of January rights or replacement feasibility across all three hyperscalers. Later changes warrant caution without resolving the historical claim. Partial support and missing evidence do not establish either the whole claim or its contradiction.
